global_insights:
Here are four concise, actionable business insights from the K-Means clustering:

• **Sales Performance Variance**: The three clusters exhibit distinct sales performance patterns. Cluster 0 has the highest sales volume (46.8%), followed by Cluster 1 (42.6%), and Cluster 2 (10.6%). This suggests that some customers or products are performing significantly better than others, indicating opportunities for targeted marketing and optimization.

• **Product Price Elasticity**: The clusters differ in price elasticity, with Cluster 0 having the highest unit prices and log1p_unit_price values, indicating a higher sensitivity to price changes. In contrast, Cluster 2 has lower prices, suggesting a more elastic demand curve. This insight can inform pricing strategies and promotions tailored to specific customer segments.

• **Customer Loyalty**: The cluster distribution reveals differences in customer loyalty. Cluster 0 customers are the most loyal, with a higher number of rows (28,083) compared to Clusters 1 and 2. This suggests that retaining these high-value customers is crucial for business growth. Conversely, Cluster 2 customers may require more attention to re-engage them.

• **Store Performance**: The clustering highlights store performance disparities. Cluster 0 stores have the highest sales volume (46.8%), while Cluster 2 stores have significantly lower sales (10.6%). This indicates that some stores are underperforming and may benefit from targeted support, training, or operational improvements to boost sales and customer engagement.
